consensus.consensusInference: The dispersion has collapsed to near-unanimity. IRI's mid-July ensemble has 23 of 26 models forecasting a very strong peak (≥+2.0°C) at OND 2026, with every single model maintaining El Niño throughout the forecast — described by IRI as exceptional model agreement. The remaining debate is narrow and specific: whether 2026 beats the 2015–16 record (+2.6°C ONI). ECMWF and CFSv2 point beyond +3°C, which would; more conservative reads and the RONI lens argue it joins rather than leads the Super club. When the models agree this tightly, the event is settled — only its magnitude ceiling is open.

timeline.inference: Read the shape carefully: this is the probability that El Niño is present in each month, not its strength. It sits near-certain (98–99%) through autumn and winter 2026, then declines through spring–summer 2027 — that fall is the expected end-of-event decay, not a weakening now. El Niño peaks in NH winter and fades the following spring; the ensembles project weakening into spring 2027. Meanwhile the strength probability is at its ceiling (81% very-strong). Both hold: near-certain to persist through the 2026–27 winter, very likely to peak very strong, and expected to decay through 2027.
